messages:
marta: heads up — seeing a spike of `resume` failures with 403 from cloud-proxy in eu-west-1 when clients try to resume SSE streams. Not seeing same for us-east. sample log: ```ERROR: resume validation failed status=403 proxy_id=cp-eu-3 session_id=abc123 opaque_salt_missing``` Anyone seen this pattern?
ajay: hm, 403 on resume usually means token not matching server-side salt. Could be the proxy lost its salt on restart and resumed sessions still carry old mac. Did you correlate with proxy restarts?
marta: yep — dozens of cp-eu-3 restarts around 08:23 UTC. But clients kept trying resume, got 403s and then fell back to full new stream. Billing/console shows double attempts but only one accepted stream.
oliver: that lines up. Proxies persist salt in mem only. When K8s node evicts pod we rotate salt. Resume tokens are MAC'd with that salt — if salt changes, resume will 403.
sophie: console telemetry also shows resume_success_rate for eu-west dropped from 99.8% -> 88% during the window. The resume metric we show in per-route dashboard doesn't break down by error code though. Hard to tell 403 vs network.
marta: repro curl for anyone who wants to try locally: ```curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <resume-token>" "https://api.redwood.test/stream/resume"``` response contains `HTTP/1.1 403` + body `{"err":"resume_invalid"}`.
ajay: proposal: change reconnect flow to 1) if resume returns 403, attempt a non-resume (fresh stream) automatically but mark it as `resume_fallback=true` and do NOT charge resume_quota. Emit metric `resume_403_fallbacks`. 2) add probe counter `proxy_salt_rotations` and surface in console.
oliver: +1 for metric, but auto-fallback can cause duplication if clients replay events. We need dedupe window server-side keyed by `session_client_id` and `last_event_id` to avoid repeating tokens to client. Also need to consider token expiration semantics (some tokens could be legitimately revoked).
sophie: from console UX POV we should make the fallback opt-in behind a rollout flag so we can enable for eu-west first. Add a console toggle per-region: "auto-resume-fallback" and a column in the stream route table for `resume_success_rate` and `resume_403_rate`.
marta: good call. Also, can we tag fallback sessions in traces so ops can quickly see where fallback happened? Right now trace shows only final accepted stream.
ajay: yes — add trace annotation `resume.fallback=403` and emit logs at INFO with `fallback=true` and `dedupe_window_ms=2000`.
oliver: implementation detail: where to perform fallback? At proxy layer or control plane? Proxy has fastest path but less visibility. Control plane can make billing decisions. My vote: proxy should attempt fallback but hit a control-plane endpoint to mark `no-charge` for that resume attempt.
sophie: that split sounds complex for rollout. Could first implement fallback in upstream aggregator (edge) with console flag and conservative dedupe, then refactor charge logic. For rollout we'll want a canary check marked in console.
marta: ok next steps: (1) ajay to spike proxy-level fallback + metric (2) oliver to design dedupe header `X-Resume-Dedupe: <last-event-id>` and server handling (3) sophie to add console flag + dashboard column + trace annotation mapping. I'll create tickets.
ajay: spike PR incoming, will include tests: unit for `resume->403` -> fallback path, integration with metrics stub, and an e2e with a simulated proxy salt rotation.
oliver: I'll draft the dedupe design doc and share later today.
sophie: I'll add dashboard mocks and a small product note for support agents explaining why a resume 403 might be harmless if fallback happened.
deploy-bot: canary rollout for `edge/resume-fallback` scheduled for 2024-09-12T14:00Z to 10% eu-west. :white_check_mark:
marta: thanks everyone. If you hit more repros, drop them here (headers, `proxy_id`, `session_id`). We'll coordinate tickets and set the console flag after the canary succeeds. :thumbsup:
